name: Abilene DC 1 gas line (Taylor County)
monitor_reason: No source that names this pipeline ties it to a data center, so the data center tie is only inferred from the operator name. It may also be in-fence plant piping, which is out of scope.
researcher_notes: The Texas Railroad Commission new construction report for 2025 (item 25-NC-074, received March 19, 2025) lists Abilene DC 1, LLC, Taylor County, a natural gas transmission line of 3.07 miles and 16 inches, new system, start March 24, 2025. The T-4 permit number was still pending on the report. The report does not mention data centers. A compute atlas page for the Crusoe Abilene site says Abilene DC 1, LLC does business as Crusoe Energy Systems and holds the state air permit for the on-site gas turbines at the Stargate Abilene campus. That page does not mention this pipeline. The Railroad Commission operator list for April 2026 shows Abilene DC 1, LLC with an Abilene DC 1 Pipeline of only 0.81 miles and the Goodnight Gas Pipeline, so the 3.07 mile line may have been reduced, split, or built as short plant piping inside the site. Not an existing row: the roster has Hugh Brinson Gas Pipeline, Abilene Laterals (P8318), which is an Energy Transfer project. Not found: any filing, press story or company release that says what this line connects or that it serves the campus. A reader could reasonably guess that the owner name points to the campus, but that is not a stated tie, so the data center tag is left blank. Worth rechecking if the T-4 record or a Crusoe or Energy Transfer document describes the line. No entity match for the owner name in the ownership list.
